name: Monotransitive Transfer with To
pattern: VP[Head:V + Theme NP + PP[to + recipient NP]]

entry.name: Monotransitive Transfer with To
entry.pattern: VP[Head:V + Theme NP + PP[to + recipient NP]]

1.definition: Packages a transferred item as direct object and its intended recipient as a to-phrase.

relatedConstructions.notes: Send licenses both frames. Other verbs, including explain in mainstream standard English, select only the to frame in this sense.

projection.target: The Theme can be the ordinary passive subject, and certain verbs such as explain allow a recipient to-phrase while resisting double objects in mainstream standard usage.
projection.evidence: See the cited discussion and the constructed illustration.

curious.title: Passing something to someone with to
curious.summary: A verb can name the thing passed along, followed by a to-phrase naming who it is meant for.
curious.body:
In Kim sent the keys to Lee, the keys are what is passed along and Lee is the person they are meant for. The thing comes right after the verb, and the receiver comes in a phrase beginning with to.

Some verbs, such as send, also allow a version with the receiver first and no to: Kim sent Lee the keys. Other verbs allow only the to version. According to this dictionary, explain is one of these in mainstream standard English. The dictionary marks this account as provisional.

examples.text: She [explained the rules to the class].

curious.try: Say Kim sent the keys to Lee, then say Kim sent Lee the keys. Now try the same two moves with explained the rules to the class.

teacher.summary: Helps explain verbs of transfer that take a direct object plus a to-phrase for the recipient.
teacher.explain: The pattern is a monotransitive VP: the head verb, a Theme noun phrase as direct object, and a prepositional phrase with to whose noun phrase is the recipient. It is a specialization of the monotransitive VP. Send licenses this frame and the double-object frame, so the two alternate. Other verbs, including explain in mainstream standard English, select only the to frame in this sense. The Theme can be the ordinary passive subject. This dictionary marks its analysis provisional, so present verb-by-verb licensing as something to check, not predict.
teacher.terms: Dative alternation is sometimes used as a textbook name for the choice between the to-phrase form and the double-object form.

examples.text: She [explained the rules to the class].

contrasts.text: Kim sent the keys to Lee.

contrasts.note: Double-object frame, also licensed by send.

watch_for: A learner might assume every verb that takes a to-phrase can also take two objects, though this dictionary says explain selects only the to frame.
A learner might treat the to-phrase as an object, when the Theme is the direct object.
teacher.activity: Give students verb cards (send, explain, give). They write one sentence per verb with a to-phrase, then test whether a double-object version also works, and sort the verbs.

child.hook: What do you say when you hand the keys to someone?
child.explain: Some sentences name what is passed first. Then they say who it is for, starting with to. Kim sent the keys to Lee.
child.play: Pass a small object around a circle. Each player says what they did, like "I passed the ball to Sam."
